description:
Programme or Project Overview

Lund University invites applications for a doctoral student position in Technology and Society within the MSCA REGULAIRE doctoral network. The project studies regulatory learning and supervisory competence in the implementation of the EU AI Act, examining how supervisory authorities build the knowledge, routines and organisational capacity needed to govern artificial intelligence. The doctoral candidate will investigate how regulators learn across cases and sectors, and how supervisory competence develops in practice as AI oversight becomes a legal obligation across Europe.

REGULAIRE is a Marie Sklodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) doctoral network bringing together universities, regulators and civil-society partners across several European countries. The doctoral position at Lund is a salaried appointment under the Swedish collective agreement, and network membership adds structured training schools, secondments with partner organisations and regular joint supervision. The position suits a candidate who wants to work at the intersection of law, technology and public administration with a European research community.

Candidate profile and network training

Applicants hold a master's degree in law, science and technology studies, public administration, artificial intelligence or a related field, and can combine doctrinal or empirical analysis with an interest in how regulation actually works. Strong written English is required, and experience with qualitative or comparative methods is an advantage. Applications run through Lund University's Varbi portal with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter, following the MSCA mobility rules that apply to doctoral candidates in the network.

Highlights

  • Doctoral position in the MSCA REGULAIRE doctoral network
  • Regulatory learning under the EU AI Act
  • Research on supervisory authorities and AI governance
  • Salaried employment per the Swedish collective agreement
  • Network training schools and secondments across Europe
  • Interdisciplinary environment at Lund University
